name: American History
description: The United States from the first colonies to the twenty-first century: revolution, civil war, civil rights and the road to superpower.

checkpoints.name: The colonies
checkpoints.note: English settlers found Virginia in 1607 and Plymouth in 1620. By the middle of the eighteenth century thirteen colonies line the Atlantic coast, many of them built on the labour of enslaved Africans.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and a new nation
checkpoints.note: Protests against British taxes grow into war. The colonies declare independence in 1776, win it in 1783 and write a constitution in 1787. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 doubles the country's size.

checkpoints.name: Westward growth and slavery
checkpoints.note: Settlers push west, Native nations are forced off their land, and war with Mexico adds the Southwest and California. Each new territory sharpens the quarrel over slavery.

checkpoints.name: Civil War and Reconstruction
checkpoints.note: Eleven Southern states leave the Union and four years of war follow. Slavery is abolished in 1865, and the country struggles over the rights of the freed people.

checkpoints.name: Industry, Depression and world wars
checkpoints.note: Railways, factories and millions of immigrants turn the United States into the largest economy in the world. The crash of 1929 brings the Great Depression, and Pearl Harbor brings the country into the Second World War.

checkpoints.name: Superpower
checkpoints.note: The Cold War, the civil rights movement, the Moon landing, Vietnam and Watergate shape the second half of the century. The attacks of 11 September 2001 open a new era.
